description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

selected_model_families.rationale: ECG data is inherently sequential; 1D convolutions effectively extract local morphological features while maintaining parameter efficiency, which is critical for the small sample size relative to input length.
Provided as a simple baseline for numeric vector data. Since features are sequentially indexed, it serves as a non-temporal reference model.

uncertainty_notes: Sampling frequency (Hz) is unknown, making it difficult to determine the appropriate kernel size for specific ECG waveforms (e.g., QRS complex).
Origin of 56 duplicate rows is unknown; they may be segments from the same patient, risking data leakage if not handled before splitting.
The 2,500 sequence length is quite long for a small sample size; there is a significant risk of the model memorizing noise.
handoff_notes: Reshape input from (2500,) to (2500, 1) for cnn1d architectures.
Recommend using StratifiedKFold cross-validation to ensure reliable evaluation on the limited sample size.
Ensure global average pooling is used after CNN layers to drastically reduce parameter count before the final dense layer.
Strictly enforce weight decay (e.g., 1e-4) to combat overfitting.
